A1.justification: Both PDFs describe A3D. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched despite additions and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on 15 prompt pairs and 26 structure-preserving transformations, quantitative ablations, hybridization examples and a RichDreamer implementation.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds ablation quality measurements, regularization sensitivity, diversity and prompt-robustness examples, and transformations of image-derived models.

M1.justification: The latent-conditioned neural field, interpolated text embeddings, SDS and normal regularization, hybridization, and structure-preserving transformation procedures remain unchanged. The CRM examples supply new input meshes to the existing Section 4.3 procedure.

E1.justification: The original 15 prompt pairs and 26 transformation cases remain. Appendix E adds limited qualitative coverage of controlled prompt paraphrases and transformations of meshes reconstructed from images using CRM, extending input conditions within the existing 3D asset domains.

E2.justification: MVEdit, LucidDreamer, GaussianEditor and the original A–F ablation configurations remain. Figure 9 adds the weaker-plausibility-regularization comparator G, and Figure 11 includes a MVDream/A3D diversity comparison.

E3.justification: v4 extends ablation evaluation beyond DIFT to CLIP and GPTEval3D in Tables 8–9 and adds controlled prompt variations and a weaker transition-sampling configuration. The original 120-view evaluation, 90 GPTEval3D comparisons and main sampling probability of 0.5 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 already tests shared representation, transition plausibility and MLP depth. Appendices D.1–E substantially extend the analysis with quality measurements for these ablations, regularization-strength sensitivity, fixed-prompt diversity and paraphrase robustness, addressing tradeoffs and failure behavior beyond structural alignment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed counts, run-wise uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Figure 11 adds qualitative examples of generation diversity but does not document a statistical repetition or uncertainty-estimation protocol.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results in Tables 1–7 are retained. New Table 8 reports ablation CLIP scores, including means of 27.7 for A3D and 28.5 for independent MVDream. Table 9 reports A3D overall-quality preference of 33.9% against B and 68.8% against C. New qualitative results show regularization tradeoffs, limited diversity, paraphrase robustness and image-derived transformations.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, the latent-simplex formulation and the Appendix C DIFT definition are unchanged. Naming the existing sampling probability p clarifies its description; no new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs or substantive derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: jointly generating structurally aligned objects through plausible, smooth transitions, enabling hybridization and structure-preserving editing, and improving asset quality over editing-based alternatives.

C2.justification: Appendices D.1–E substantially expand interpretation: they develop the existing alignment–realism tradeoff, explain the limited role of MLP depth through hash-grid capacity, and attribute restricted diversity to strong guidance and backbone training. The ethics statement adds specific inherited-data limitations. The original static-object limitation remains.

D1.justification: New Appendix B.4 discloses A100 hardware, approximately 20k iterations and 1.5 hours per generated pair, scaling budgets for additional objects, and competitor runtimes. These details were absent from v2; the existing architecture, loss weights and baseline implementation instructions largely persist.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for Instant-NGP, CRM and inherited dataset risks, while removing the Instant3D and ProlificDreamer citations and associated discussion. The central positioning against independent generation and sequential editing is retained.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work and preliminaries receive selective tightening. v4 adds a method overview, ethics and reproducibility statements, and further appendix subdivisions. The main section sequence and most method and experimental prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds the method diagram in Figure 3, five experimental figures numbered 9–13, and Tables 8–9. The original qualitative ablation moves from main-text Figure 6 to appendix Figure 8. Existing tables are regrouped, and Table 7 gains an average row repeating the previously reported aggregate results.

improvement.justification: Tables 8–9 make the quality costs of stronger alignment more assessable, while computational budgets and new sensitivity and diversity examples improve reproducibility and qualification of the findings. These are useful, targeted gains; the original comparative evidence remains unchanged, and the new robustness and application demonstrations are qualitative without statistical uncertainty reporting.
